Excellent. Now I have a complete picture. Let me compile my findings:

## **Interactive Visualization Block Generation — Complete Pipeline Report**

### **1. THE PROMPT**

**Location:** `/Users/zhangjunqiu/Documents/Primoria/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.ts`, lines 414–497

**System instruction** (line 657–660):
```
You create safe, offline, interactive educational HTML documents for sandboxed iframes. 
Return only one complete runnable HTML document. Do not return JSON or markdown.
```

**User prompt architecture** (lines 414–497):
- **Core directive:** Return single complete HTML (lines 428–435). No JSON, no markdown fences, self-contained, inline `<script>` only, offline-only.
- **Technical constraints:** HTML/CSS/vanilla JS only. No React, external libs, images, URLs, `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, WebSocket, `iframe`, `embed`, or `<script src>`. Must run in sandboxed iframe.
- **CSS guidance:** Use injected base classes (`iv-shell`, `iv-header`, `iv-card`, `iv-visual-card`, `iv-controls-card`, `iv-observation-card`, etc.) instead of writing boilerplate.
- **Design requirements:** Clean, modern, responsive layout with title area + core visualization + controls + observation/conclusion. Visual must be first thing learners notice. Concise labels over long static text.
- **Educational:** Show concept visually, not just formulas. Include short explanations. Every control must have educational purpose. Default state simple. Call `window.PrimoriaInteractive?.track?.(eventName, payload)` for meaningful learner interactions.
- **Topic-specific guidance** (lines 392–412): Detects linear function patterns (`y=ax+b`) and injects explicit requirements for slope triangles, y-intercept labels, live formula display, sliders for `a`/`b`, and animation triggers.

**Language & Template hints** (lines 415–427):
- Auto-detects Chinese text in prompt; writes labels in Simplified Chinese if found.
- Accepts optional `template` (e.g., `linear-function-graph`, `wave`, `generic`) and `experienceMode` (`simulation|graph|scenario|story`). Falls back to auto-inference if not specified.

---

### **2. FULL GENERATION PIPELINE**

**Trigger → Client API → Edge Function → Database → Renderer:**

| Stage | File | Details |
|-------|------|---------|
| **User triggers generation** | `/packages/viewer-react/src/features/editor/properties/panels/InteractiveVisualPanel.tsx` lines 160–182 | Author enters AI prompt in textarea, clicks "Generate with AI". Calls `createInteractiveVisual()` with template, language, experienceMode, surface='builder'. |
| **Client API layer** | `/packages/viewer-react/src/shared/api/viewer/interactiveVisualApi.ts` lines 171–282 | `createInteractiveVisualJob()` sends `{action:'create', prompt, template, experienceMode, language, surface}` to edge function. Client polls every 1.5s for job status. Timeout = 180s. Falls back to fallback HTML if `allowFallback=true` and fails. |
| **Edge function: model & config** | `/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.ts` lines 7–15 | Model: `gemini-2.0-flash` (default), fallback to `gemini-2.5-flash-latest`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.0-flash`. Max output: 16,384 tokens. Temperature: 0.45 (deterministic). |
| **Generation attempt logic** | Lines 645–706 | Try each model in fallback order. For each, call Gemini API with system + user prompt. Extract candidate texts. Parse for HTML. Validate offline. Build artifact. On failure: retry with repair instructions (max 2 repair attempts for validation errors; exponential backoff for transient). |
| **Validation** | Lines 357–379 | Must be complete HTML. No `<script src>`, no module scripts, no `<link href>`, no `<iframe|embed|object>`, no `fetch|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|import()`, no external URLs (except W3C SVG/XLink namespaces). |
| **Artifact structure** | Lines 586–606, type in `interactiveVisualApi.ts` lines 22–35 | Returns: `{version, engine, title, description, template, experienceMode, themeTone, aiPrompt, generatedHtml}`. Title/description extracted from HTML `<title>` or `.iv-subtitle` or fallback. Template/mode inferred from prompt if not provided. |
| **Storage** | `/supabase/migrations/20260511000001_interactive_visual_generation_jobs.sql` | Stored in `interactive_visual_generation_jobs` table: `id` (UUID), `user_id`, `status` ('queued'|'running'|'succeeded'|'failed'), `prompt`, `request_payload` (JSONB), `result_artifact` (JSONB), `error_history` (JSONB array), `attempt_count`, `next_attempt_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `completed_at`. |
| **Rendering (viewer)** | `/packages/viewer-react/src/shared/interactive-visual/` | `InteractiveVisualRenderer.tsx` dispatches to `HtmlIframeInteractiveVisualRenderer`, `PhysicsCanvasWaveRenderer`, or `TrustedInteractiveVisualPlaceholders` based on engine type. HTML blocks use `InteractiveVisualEmbed.tsx`: injects bridge script, wraps in `srcDoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts"`. |

---

### **3. OUTPUT FORMAT & SCHEMA**

**Artifact returned to client** (type `InteractiveVisualArtifact`):
```typescript
{
  version: '1';
  engine: 'gemini-html5' | 'fallback-html5' | 'interactive-html5';
  template: 'linear-function-graph' | 'wave' | 'pendulum' | 'projectile' | 'generic';
  experienceMode: 'simulation' | 'graph' | 'scenario' | 'story';
  title: string;
  description?: string;
  aiPrompt?: string;
  generatedHtml: string; // Complete <!doctype html> ... </html>
  themeTone?: string; // E.g., 'primoria-system', 'sky', 'sand', 'sage'
  runtime?: Record<string, unknown>; // For physics-canvas: { simulation: 'wave', params: {amplitude, frequency, phase, speed} }
}
```

**Supported renderer engines:**
- **`html-iframe`** (aliases: `interactive-html5`, `gemini-html5`, `fallback-html5`): Sandboxed iframe with user-generated or fallback HTML.
- **`physics-canvas`**: Trusted canvas renderer for wave simulations only (no generated HTML executed).
- **`r3f-cell-3d`**: Trusted 3D cell explorer placeholder (no generated HTML executed).

**Fallback visual templates** (auto-generated if generation fails):
- Wave/cosine curve explorer
- Pendulum lab
- Projectile lab
- Generic concept explorer

---

### **4. CONSTRAINTS**

**Sandboxing:**
- Iframe `sandbox="allow-scripts"` only—no forms, popups, top-level navigation.
- All HTML must be complete, self-contained documents.
- No external resource loading (images, fonts, stylesheets, scripts).

**Size limits:**
- Max generation output: 16,384 tokens.
- Individual HTML doc: implicit from Supabase row limit (~1MB).

**Network:**
- Fully offline. No fetch, WebSocket, XMLHttpRequest.
- SVG/XLink W3C namespace URLs are whitelisted for `createElementNS()` but not actual HTTP requests.

**Retry/error handling:**
- Transient (429, 5xx): max 4 exponential backoff retries (2s, 6s, 15s, 40s).
- Validation (HTML extraction/validation failure): max 2 repair attempts using error messages as repair instructions.
- Fatal (malformed response, auth failure): no retry.

---

### **5. TEST CONTRACT**

| Test File | Key Assertions |
|-----------|---|
| `/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.test.ts` (lines 29–142) | Prompt contains "complete HTML", "Do not return JSON", required CSS classes. HTML extraction from markdown fences. Base styles injected. Offline validation rejects `<script src>`, modules, external stylesheets, `fetch`, external URLs. |
| `/packages/viewer-react/test/interactiveVisualApi.test.ts` (lines 34–144) | Missing function → readable error. Auth required. Job creation + polling. Artifact structure. Fallback on 5xx without `allowFallback: false`. |
| `/packages/viewer-react/test/interactiveVisualPanel.test.tsx` (lines 48–113) | Form input → generation call with correct payload. Block content updated with artifact fields (engine, template, title, description, aiPrompt, generatedHtml, themeTone, experienceMode). |
| `/packages/viewer-react/test/interactiveVisualRenderer.test.tsx` (lines 32–160) | Legacy `generatedHtml` → iframe renderer. Engine aliases map to HTML iframe. `r3f-cell-3d` → trusted placeholder. `physics-canvas` → canvas renderer, ignores generated HTML. Unsupported engine → error state. |

---

### **6. PROMPT WEAKNESSES & UPGRADE OPPORTUNITIES**

1. **Vague visual quality bar:** Prompt says "clean, modern" but no exemplars, design patterns, or specific color/layout constraints. Gemini outputs vary in polish.
2. **No explicit progressive enhancement:** Prompt doesn't guide graceful fallback for slow/mobile learners or progressive disclosure of controls.
3. **Minimal learner outcome specification:** No requirement to measure understanding or store learner state beyond analytics events. Observation panel is static template-driven, not adaptive.
4. **Limited topic specificity:** Only linear functions get detailed scaffolding. Other STEM topics (waves, circuits, collisions) reuse generic guidance.
5. **Weak interaction design contract:** Prompt doesn't require pedagogically sequenced controls, danger zones, or explicit cause-effect animation triggers. "Visually obvious" is subjective.
6. **No accessibility guidance:** No mention of keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, color contrast, high-contrast mode, or captions for sighted users.
7. **Missing repairability signals:** When Gemini fails validation, repair instructions only include error message—no examples of what *correct* HTML looks like for that topic.

**Suggested upgrades:** Add exemplar HTML snippets (linear-function graph, wave explorer), hard constraints on min interaction steps, accessibility checklist, learner-outcome-focused observation logic, and topic-specific visual patterns library.

Return only one complete runnable HTML document. Do not return JSON or markdown.
```

- **Core directive:** Return single complete HTML (lines 428–435). No JSON, no markdown fences, self-contained, inline `<script>` only, offline-only.
- **Technical constraints:** HTML/CSS/vanilla JS only. No React, external libs, images, URLs, `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, WebSocket, `iframe`, `embed`, or `<script src>`. Must run in sandboxed iframe.
- **CSS guidance:** Use injected base classes (`iv-shell`, `iv-header`, `iv-card`, `iv-visual-card`, `iv-controls-card`, `iv-observation-card`, etc.) instead of writing boilerplate.
- **Design requirements:** Clean, modern, responsive layout with title area + core visualization + controls + observation/conclusion. Visual must be first thing learners notice. Concise labels over long static text.
- **Educational:** Show concept visually, not just formulas. Include short explanations. Every control must have educational purpose. Default state simple. Call `window.PrimoriaInteractive?.track?.(eventName, payload)` for meaningful learner interactions.
- **Topic-specific guidance** (lines 392–412): Detects linear function patterns (`y=ax+b`) and injects explicit requirements for slope triangles, y-intercept labels, live formula display, sliders for `a`/`b`, and animation triggers.

**Language & Template hints** (lines 415–427):
- Auto-detects Chinese text in prompt; writes labels in Simplified Chinese if found.
- Accepts optional `template` (e.g., `linear-function-graph`, `wave`, `generic`) and `experienceMode` (`simulation|graph|scenario|story`). Falls back to auto-inference if not specified.

---

### **2. FULL GENERATION PIPELINE**

**Trigger → Client API → Edge Function → Database → Renderer:**

| Stage | File | Details |
|-------|------|---------|
| **User triggers generation** | `/packages/viewer-react/src/features/editor/properties/panels/InteractiveVisualPanel.tsx` lines 160–182 | Author enters AI prompt in textarea, clicks "Generate with AI". Calls `createInteractiveVisual()` with template, language, experienceMode, surface='builder'. |
| **Client API layer** | `/packages/viewer-react/src/shared/api/viewer/interactiveVisualApi.ts` lines 171–282 | `createInteractiveVisualJob()` sends `{action:'create', prompt, template, experienceMode, language, surface}` to edge function. Client polls every 1.5s for job status. Timeout = 180s. Falls back to fallback HTML if `allowFallback=true` and fails. |
| **Edge function: model & config** | `/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.ts` lines 7–15 | Model: `gemini-2.0-flash` (default), fallback to `gemini-2.5-flash-latest`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.0-flash`. Max output: 16,384 tokens. Temperature: 0.45 (deterministic). |

Build artifact. On failure: retry with repair instructions (max 2 repair attempts for validation errors; exponential backoff for transient). |
| **Validation** | Lines 357–379 | Must be complete HTML. No `<script src>`, no module scripts, no `<link href>`, no `<iframe|embed|object>`, no `fetch|XMLHttpRequest|WebSocket|import()`, no external URLs (except W3C SVG/XLink namespaces). |
| **Artifact structure** | Lines 586–606, type in `interactiveVisualApi.ts` lines 22–35 | Returns: `{version, engine, title, description, template, experienceMode, themeTone, aiPrompt, generatedHtml}`. HTML blocks use `InteractiveVisualEmbed.tsx`: injects bridge script, wraps in `srcDoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts"`. |

---

### **3. OUTPUT FORMAT & SCHEMA**

**Artifact returned to client** (type `InteractiveVisualArtifact`):
```typescript
{
  version: '1';
  engine: 'gemini-html5' | 'fallback-html5' | 'interactive-html5';
  template: 'linear-function-graph' | 'wave' | 'pendulum' | 'projectile' | 'generic';
  experienceMode: 'simulation' | 'graph' | 'scenario' | 'story';
  title: string;
  description?: string;
  aiPrompt?: string;
  generatedHtml: string; // Complete <!doctype html> ... </html>
  themeTone?: string; // E.g., 'primoria-system', 'sky', 'sand', 'sage'
  runtime?: Record<string, unknown>; // For physics-canvas: { simulation: 'wave', params: {amplitude, frequency, phase, speed} }
}
```

**Supported renderer engines:**
- **`html-iframe`** (aliases: `interactive-html5`, `gemini-html5`, `fallback-html5`): Sandboxed iframe with user-generated or fallback HTML.
- **`physics-canvas`**: Trusted canvas renderer for wave simulations only (no generated HTML executed).
- **`r3f-cell-3d`**: Trusted 3D cell explorer placeholder (no generated HTML executed).

**Fallback visual templates** (auto-generated if generation fails):
- Wave/cosine curve explorer
- Pendulum lab
- Projectile lab
- Generic concept explorer

---

### **4. CONSTRAINTS**

**Sandboxing:**
- Iframe `sandbox="allow-scripts"` only—no forms, popups, top-level navigation.
- All HTML must be complete, self-contained documents.
- No external resource loading (images, fonts, stylesheets, scripts).

**Size limits:**
- Max generation output: 16,384 tokens.
- Individual HTML doc: implicit from Supabase row limit (~1MB).

**Network:**
- Fully offline. No fetch, WebSocket, XMLHttpRequest.
- SVG/XLink W3C namespace URLs are whitelisted for `createElementNS()` but not actual HTTP requests.

**Retry/error handling:**
- Transient (429, 5xx): max 4 exponential backoff retries (2s, 6s, 15s, 40s).
- Validation (HTML extraction/validation failure): max 2 repair attempts using error messages as repair instructions.
- Fatal (malformed response, auth failure): no retry.

---

### **5. TEST CONTRACT**

| Test File | Key Assertions |
|-----------|---|
| `/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.test.ts` (lines 29–142) | Prompt contains "complete HTML", "Do not return JSON", required CSS classes. HTML extraction from markdown fences. Base styles injected. Offline validation rejects `<script src>`, modules, external stylesheets, `fetch`, external URLs. |
| `/packages/viewer-react/test/interactiveVisualApi.test.ts` (lines 34–144) | Missing function → readable error. Auth required. Job creation + polling. Artifact structure. Fallback on 5xx without `allowFallback: false`. |
| `/packages/viewer-react/test/interactiveVisualPanel.test.tsx` (lines 48–113) | Form input → generation call with correct payload. Block content updated with artifact fields (engine, template, title, description, aiPrompt, generatedHtml, themeTone, experienceMode). |
| `/packages/viewer-react/test/interactiveVisualRenderer.test.tsx` (lines 32–160) | Legacy `generatedHtml` → iframe renderer. Engine aliases map to HTML iframe. `r3f-cell-3d` → trusted placeholder. `physics-canvas` → canvas renderer, ignores generated HTML. Unsupported engine → error state. |

---

### **6. PROMPT WEAKNESSES & UPGRADE OPPORTUNITIES**

1. **Vague visual quality bar:** Prompt says "clean, modern" but no exemplars, design patterns, or specific color/layout constraints. Gemini outputs vary in polish.
2. **No explicit progressive enhancement:** Prompt doesn't guide graceful fallback for slow/mobile learners or progressive disclosure of controls.
3. **Minimal learner outcome specification:** No requirement to measure understanding or store learner state beyond analytics events. Observation panel is static template-driven, not adaptive.
4. **Limited topic specificity:** Only linear functions get detailed scaffolding. Other STEM topics (waves, circuits, collisions) reuse generic guidance.
5. **Weak interaction design contract:** Prompt doesn't require pedagogically sequenced controls, danger zones, or explicit cause-effect animation triggers. "Visually obvious" is subjective.
6. **No accessibility guidance:** No mention of keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, color contrast, high-contrast mode, or captions for sighted users.
7. **Missing repairability signals:** When Gemini fails validation, repair instructions only include error message—no examples of what *correct* HTML looks like for that topic.

**Suggested upgrades:** Add exemplar HTML snippets (linear-function graph, wave explorer), hard constraints on min interaction steps, accessibility checklist, learner-outcome-focused observation logic, and topic-specific visual patterns library.

What's Distinctive / Noteworthy 1. **Skills-based architecture** — Instead of one monolithic system prompt, OpenGenerativeUI loads specific SKILL.md files on-demand via LangChain Deep Agents. This prevents broken-looking output. 6. **Detailed component patterns** — The SVG Skill includes copy-paste templates for single-line nodes, two-line nodes, connectors, and text sizing logic. Designers don't re-invent; they extend templates. 7. **Deliberate constraint on libraries** — Only Three.js, D3.js, GSAP, and Chart.js are available. This structures the LLM's output and prevents hallucination. 3. **Inject design system CSS variables** — Pre-inject theme colors and typography tokens so all outputs are consistent and light/dark-aware. 4. **Provide copy-paste component patterns** — Include SVG node templates, HTML card templates, and sizing formulas so the LLM doesn't invent layouts. 5. **Be explicit about quality** — State the floor: "portfolio-ready, polished, no proof-of-concept." This shifts LLM behavior. 6. **Forbid fakes (3D, animations, effects)** — Tell the LLM what libraries it can't use (no CSS 3D fakes, no unstyled "raw" output). Constraints enable quality. 7. **Document the decision matrix** — Provide a table mapping user intents to output types (data-driven → Chart.js, spatial → SVG, etc.). This guides the LLM's choice.

questions.question: OpenGenerativeUI allows Three.js / D3 / GSAP / Chart.js inside the iframe via an ES import map (loaded from a CDN allowlist). Our current sandbox is strictly offline — no <script src>, no external URLs, no fetch. Three.js, D3, and GSAP are the main reason their 3D/animation output looks portfolio-ready. Which path should the new design take?

options.label: Allow whitelisted CDN libs (Recommended)
options.description: Add a small CDN allowlist (esm.sh / jsdelivr) for Three.js, D3, GSAP, Chart.js. Keep iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" but lift the offline-only rule. Required to match OpenGenerativeUI's visual quality.

options.label: Bundle libs locally, no CDN
options.description: Ship Three.js / D3 / GSAP as local assets served from our origin. Same visual capability, no CDN trust. Slower to set up; larger bundle.

options.label: Stay strictly offline
options.description: Keep current no-external-scripts rule. Rewrite the prompt to push vanilla JS + SVG / Canvas2D quality up, but accept that 3D and rich data viz will remain limited.

questions.question: OpenGenerativeUI's pipeline is multi-step: plan_visualization tool call → render tool call → narrate. Our current pipeline is a single Gemini call that returns HTML. Which generation flow should the new design adopt?

options.label: Two-step: plan → render (Recommended)
options.description: First call returns a structured plan JSON (approach, technology, 2-4 key elements, palette, interactions). Second call renders HTML conditioned on the plan. Better consistency; ~2× latency / cost.

options.label: Single-pass, better prompt
options.description: Keep one Gemini call but bake the planning structure into the prompt as a required preamble in the response. Faster + cheaper, weaker enforcement.

options.label: Two-step with author preview of the plan
options.description: Author sees the plan in the Builder panel and can edit/approve before render. Highest control; adds UX work in InteractiveVisualPanel.tsx.

questions.question: OpenGenerativeUI keeps its system prompt small and loads topic-specific SKILL.md files on demand (svg-diagrams, advanced-visualization, etc.). Our current prompt is one monolithic string in index.ts. How modular should the new prompt be?

options.label: Modular skills, loaded per template (Recommended)
options.description: Split into core-system.md + per-template skills (linear-function.md, wave.md, 3d-scene.md, chart.md, generic.md). Edge function picks 1-2 to inject based on detected template. Easier to iterate on each topic independently.

options.label: One big rewritten prompt
options.description: Keep prompt as a single string in index.ts but fully rewrite with the OpenGenerativeUI quality bar, design tokens, and component patterns. Less infra change.

questions.question: Should the new prompt enforce a design-token CSS-variable system (like OpenGenerativeUI's --color-text-primary, --color-background-secondary) with light/dark mode, or keep our current iv-* CSS class system?

options.label: Add CSS-variable tokens + keep iv-* classes (Recommended)
options.description: Inject both: theme CSS variables (light/dark) AND the existing iv-shell / iv-card classes. Prompt instructs the AI to use variables for colors and iv-* classes for layout primitives. Backward-compatible.

options.label: Replace iv-* with CSS-variable tokens entirely
options.description: Drop the iv-* class system, mirror OpenGenerativeUI's design-token approach exactly. Cleanest result but requires updating existing fallback templates and the renderer's injected baseline CSS.

options.label: Keep iv-* only, no CSS variables
options.description: Make the prompt tighter around the existing iv-* primitives. Smallest change; no theming improvement.

# Primoria Interactive Visual — Two-Step Generation Upgrade Plan

## 1. Context

The current `viewer-ai-interactive-visual` edge function makes a single Gemini call that must invent both *design intent* and *runnable HTML* in one shot, with a strict offline sandbox and no CDN libs. Output quality is capped by Gemini's ability to one-pass both jobs and by the absence of richer rendering libraries. We are adopting CopilotKit / OpenGenerativeUI patterns: (a) a structured **plan** step that thinks about approach, palette, interactions, accessibility before any code; (b) a richer runtime that allows ESM imports of `three`, `d3`, `gsap`, `chart.js/auto` from a tight CDN allowlist; (c) modular template **skills** injected only when relevant; (d) a design-token CSS layer alongside the existing `iv-*` layout primitives. Generation cost roughly doubles (two Gemini calls per job), accepted as the price for substantially higher visual fidelity. The artifact stays backward compatible — `plan` is purely additive in `result_artifact`.

## 2. Architecture (ASCII)

```
client (Builder / AI-Tutor)
   │  POST action=create
   ▼
edge function: viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.ts
   │
   ├── jobs table row created (status=queued)
   │
   └── processSingleJob()
         │
         ├── Step A: generateInteractivePlan(payload)
         │     - prompt = coreSystem + planInstructions + user ask
         │     - Gemini #1 returns JSON
         │     - parsePlan() → PlanSchema (zod)
         │     - on parse fail → retry once with repair note
         │
         ├── Step B: generateInteractiveHtml(payload, plan)
         │     - skills = pickSkills(plan.technology, plan.template)
         │     - prompt = coreSystem + selected skills + designTokens
         │               + iv-* CSS guide + plan(JSON) + user ask
         │               + (optional) validator-repair note
         │     - Gemini #2 returns HTML
         │     - extractInteractiveVisualHtml()
         │     - injectInteractiveVisualBaseStyles()  ← now also injects design-token block
         │     - validateOfflineHtml() ← UPDATED allowlist
         │     - on validation fail → loop once with errors + locked plan
         │
         └── result_artifact = {
               version, engine, title, description,
               template, experienceMode, themeTone, aiPrompt,
               generatedHtml,
               plan: { ...PlanSchema }    ← NEW additive field
             }

client poll (existing) reads resultArtifact unchanged; plan ignored.
Renderer (InteractiveVisualEmbed) unchanged — iframe sandbox still allow-scripts.
```

## 3. File-by-file changes

**New files** (Deno-friendly TypeScript string exports inside the edge function dir):

- `/Users/zhangjunqiu/Documents/Primoria/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/prompts/coreSystem.ts` — exports `CORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (string).

- `/Users/zhangjunqiu/Documents/Primoria/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/prompts/skills/linearFunction.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/wave.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/threeDScene.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/chart.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/generic.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/index.ts` — exports `pickSkillsForTemplate(template, planTechnology) → string[]`.
- `…/planSchema.ts` — exports the zod `PlanSchema`, `type Plan`, and `parsePlanText(raw: string) → Plan`.
- `…/planStep.ts` — exports `generateInteractivePlan(payload, repairNote?) → Promise<Plan>` (wraps Gemini call #1).
- `…/renderStep.ts` — exports `generateInteractiveHtml(payload, plan, repairErrors[]) → Promise<artifact>` (wraps Gemini call #2; replaces the body of the current `generateInteractiveVisual`).
- (new test) `…/index.test.ts` already exists — add cases; also add `…/planSchema.test.ts` for the parser.

**Modified files**:

  - Add `INTERACTIVE_VISUAL_TWO_STEP_ENABLED` env-flag read at top (default `'true'`).

If we skip this, do nothing — the server output is trusted and the client validator only runs on raw artifact reload.

## 4. Plan-step JSON schema

```ts
// supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/planSchema.ts
import { z } from 'npm:zod@3.25.76';

export const PlanSchema = z.object({
  approach: z.string().min(20).max(800),          // one-paragraph design intent
  technology: z.enum(['svg', 'canvas2d', 'three', 'd3', 'chartjs', 'css-anim', 'hybrid']),
  template: z.string().min(2).max(60),            // e.g. 'linear-function', 'wave', '3d-scene'
  palette: z.object({
    mode: z.enum(['light', 'dark', 'auto']).default('auto'),
    primary: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/),
    accent: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/),
    surface: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/).optional(),
  }),
  keyElements: z.array(z.string().min(2)).min(2).max(8),  // e.g. "live formula y=ax+b", "slope triangle"
  interactions: z.array(z.object({
    control: z.string(),                          // 'slider:a', 'button:reset', 'drag:point'
    purpose: z.string(),                          // educational reason
  })).min(1).max(8),
  accessibilityNotes: z.array(z.string()).min(1).max(6),
  observationCopyHint: z.string().max(280),       // what the live observation should say
});
export type Plan = z.infer<typeof PlanSchema>;
```

Example:
```json

  "approach": "Show y = ax + b on a coordinate plane with the line redrawing live as a and b change. Highlight slope via a Δx=1, Δy=a triangle.",

  "palette": { "mode": "auto", "primary": "#2563eb", "accent": "#e4572e", "surface": "#ffffff" },
  "keyElements": ["live formula y=ax+b", "labeled axes", "slope triangle", "y-intercept marker"],
  "interactions": [
    {"control": "slider:a", "purpose": "Vary slope to feel rotation/tilt"},
    {"control": "slider:b", "purpose": "Vary intercept to feel parallel shift"},
    {"control": "button:reset", "purpose": "Return to identity line"}
  ],
  "accessibilityNotes": ["sliders have aria-labels", "contrast meets WCAG AA"],
  "observationCopyHint": "When a increases, the line rotates steeper through (0,b)."
}
```

## 5. Render-step prompt structure

Composition order (passed as the user-message text; system instruction stays the safety preamble):

1. `CORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` — global rules: complete HTML doc, no commentary, no fetch, must call `window.PrimoriaInteractive?.track`, must use injected tokens + `iv-*` classes, may use CDN allowlist via `<script type="module">` imports from esm.sh / jsdelivr only.
2. `DESIGN_TOKEN_GUIDE` — table of CSS variable names and what each means (colors, spacing, radius, font), with directive "use `var(--color-...)` for ALL color references; do not hardcode colors".
3. Selected skill prompts (`pickSkillsForTemplate(plan.template, plan.technology)`) — 1–2 of: `linearFunction`, `wave`, `threeDScene`, `chart`, `generic`.
4. Existing `iv-*` class layout guide (the structured paragraph already in `buildInteractiveVisualPrompt`).
5. Locked plan — `Plan JSON (authoritative — implement exactly):\n<json>`.
6. Author context (surface, language, title, description) and the user's original `prompt`.
7. Optional repair note (validator errors + "you must keep the plan above intact").

## 6. New validator rules

CDN allowlist (tight): `https://esm.sh/` and `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/` only. We deliberately exclude unpkg (history of arbitrary subpaths) and skypack.

Changes in `validateOfflineHtml` (current location lines 357–379 of `index.ts`):

- Drop the blanket `<script[^>]+src=` rejection; instead allow `<script type="module" src="https://esm.sh/...">` or `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/...`.
- Drop the blanket `type=module` rejection.
- Drop the blanket "no module imports" rule. **Allow** static `import ... from "https://esm.sh/..."` and `import ... from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/..."` inside module scripts. Still **forbid** `import(...)` dynamic with a non-allowlisted argument — easiest: forbid `import(` entirely (libs we allow don't need dynamic import).
- Keep forbidding `<link href=...>` for stylesheets (no CSS CDN; design tokens come from us).
- Keep forbidding `<iframe|embed|object>`.
- Keep forbidding `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`.
- Replace the "no `https?://` anywhere" check with: after stripping (a) SVG/XLink namespace URLs (already handled), (b) allowlisted CDN URLs that appear only inside `<script src=...>` or `import ... from "..."` positions, any remaining `https?://` is rejected.

Concrete regex sketch (where in `index.ts`):
```ts
const ALLOWED_CDN = /^https:\/\/(esm\.sh|cdn\.jsdelivr\.net\/npm)\//;
// In validateOfflineHtml:
//   1) Collect all <script ... src="X"> X values → each must match ALLOWED_CDN.
//   2) Collect all `import ... from "X"` X values → each must match ALLOWED_CDN.
//   3) Strip allowed-CDN URLs and SVG-namespace URLs from html → assert no remaining https?://.
//   4) Reject dynamic import(): /\bimport\s*\(/i.
//   5) Reject fetch/XHR/WebSocket as today.
```

## 8. Skill files (scope only)

- **coreSystem.ts** — Global hard rules: complete `<!doctype html>` doc, no commentary/fences, must call `window.PrimoriaInteractive?.track`, may use ESM imports only from esm.sh / jsdelivr-npm, must reference design-token variables for colors, must use `iv-*` classes for layout, must include observation card, must be keyboard-accessible.
- **linearFunction.ts** — When `template = linear-function*`: live `y = ax + b` formula bound to two sliders, axes with ticks, slope triangle Δx=1/Δy=a, y-intercept dot at (0,b), dynamic observation sentence. Prefer SVG.
- **wave.ts** — When `template = wave|trig|sin|cos`: amplitude/frequency/phase/shift sliders, animated trace, gridded axes, current-state stats panel, play/pause/reset, prefer Canvas2D or SVG.
- **threeDScene.ts** — When `plan.technology = three` or template hints 3D: import `three` from esm.sh, OrbitControls allowed, ambient + directional light, single hero mesh, optional `gsap` for transitions, fallback gracefully if WebGL absent. Bullet: must `dispose()` on unload.
- **chart.ts** — When `plan.technology = chartjs` or template = chart/bar/line/pie/scatter: import `chart.js/auto` from jsdelivr, set `responsive: true`, palette pulled from CSS variables via `getComputedStyle`, single canvas, optional second chart for comparison.
- **generic.ts** — Default catch-all: emphasize one core concept, one primary control, observation card, no dashboard padding, prefer SVG/CSS animation.

`pickSkillsForTemplate(template, technology)` rules: always include the technology-driven skill (`three` → threeDScene; `chartjs` → chart) first, then template-specific (`linear-function` → linearFunction, `wave` → wave, else generic). Cap at 2.

- **Plan parse fail** (invalid JSON or zod rejection): retry the plan step exactly once with a repair note `"Previous output was not valid JSON for the plan schema. Re-emit only the JSON object. Errors: <messages>"`. If second attempt fails, classify as `validation` and bubble through existing `processSingleJob` retry book-keeping (counts toward `MAX_VALIDATION_REPAIRS`).
- **Plan succeeds, render parse fail / no `<html>`**: classify as `validation`. On retry, **keep the plan**, append render-step repair note: `"Previous HTML missed the locked plan. Plan to honor: <JSON>. Re-emit a complete document."`.
- **Plan succeeds, render validator fail**: same as above + concrete error messages from `validateOfflineHtml`. Up to `MAX_VALIDATION_REPAIRS = 2` (existing).
- **Gemini 429/5xx on either step**: classified `transient`, existing exponential delay schedule reused.
- **Final failure**: `last_error` includes which step failed (`plan` vs `render`) and message. `result_artifact` remains null. Job marked `failed`.

# Primoria Interactive Visual — Two-Step Generation Upgrade Plan

## 1. Context

The current `viewer-ai-interactive-visual` edge function makes a single Gemini call that must invent both *design intent* and *runnable HTML* in one shot, with a strict offline sandbox and no CDN libs. Output quality is capped by Gemini's ability to one-pass both jobs and by the absence of richer rendering libraries. We are adopting CopilotKit / OpenGenerativeUI patterns: (a) a structured **plan** step that thinks about approach, palette, interactions, accessibility before any code; (b) a richer runtime that allows ESM imports of `three`, `d3`, `gsap`, `chart.js/auto` from a tight CDN allowlist; (c) modular template **skills** injected only when relevant; (d) a design-token CSS layer alongside the existing `iv-*` layout primitives. Generation cost roughly doubles (two Gemini calls per job), accepted as the price for substantially higher visual fidelity. The artifact stays backward compatible — `plan` is purely additive in `result_artifact`.

## 2. Architecture (ASCII)

```
client (Builder / AI-Tutor)
   │  POST action=create
   ▼
edge function: viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.ts
   │
   ├── jobs table row created (status=queued)
   │
   └── processSingleJob()
         │
         ├── Step A: generateInteractivePlan(payload)
         │     - prompt = coreSystem + planInstructions + user ask
         │     - Gemini #1 returns JSON
         │     - parsePlan() → PlanSchema (zod)
         │     - on parse fail → retry once with repair note
         │
         ├── Step B: generateInteractiveHtml(payload, plan)
         │     - skills = pickSkills(plan.technology, plan.template)
         │     - prompt = coreSystem + selected skills + designTokens
         │               + iv-* CSS guide + plan(JSON) + user ask
         │               + (optional) validator-repair note
         │     - Gemini #2 returns HTML
         │     - extractInteractiveVisualHtml()
         │     - injectInteractiveVisualBaseStyles()  ← now also injects design-token block
         │     - validateOfflineHtml() ← UPDATED allowlist
         │     - on validation fail → loop once with errors + locked plan
         │
         └── result_artifact = {
               version, engine, title, description,
               template, experienceMode, themeTone, aiPrompt,
               generatedHtml,
               plan: { ...PlanSchema }    ← NEW additive field
             }

client poll (existing) reads resultArtifact unchanged; plan ignored.
Renderer (InteractiveVisualEmbed) unchanged — iframe sandbox still allow-scripts.
```

## 3. File-by-file changes

**New files** (Deno-friendly TypeScript string exports inside the edge function dir):

- `/Users/zhangjunqiu/Documents/Primoria/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/prompts/coreSystem.ts` — exports `CORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (string).
- `/Users/zhangjunqiu/Documents/Primoria/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/prompts/designTokens.ts` — exports `DESIGN_TOKEN_CSS` (string) and `DESIGN_TOKEN_GUIDE` (string, names to reference from generated HTML).
- `/Users/zhangjunqiu/Documents/Primoria/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/prompts/skills/linearFunction.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/wave.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/threeDScene.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/chart.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/generic.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/index.ts` — exports `pickSkillsForTemplate(template, planTechnology) → string[]`.
- `…/planSchema.ts` — exports the zod `PlanSchema`, `type Plan`, and `parsePlanText(raw: string) → Plan`.
- `…/planStep.ts` — exports `generateInteractivePlan(payload, repairNote?) → Promise<Plan>` (wraps Gemini call #1).
- `…/renderStep.ts` — exports `generateInteractiveHtml(payload, plan, repairErrors[]) → Promise<artifact>` (wraps Gemini call #2; replaces the body of the current `generateInteractiveVisual`).
- (new test) `…/index.test.ts` already exists — add cases; also add `…/planSchema.test.ts` for the parser.

**Modified files**:

- `/Users/zhangjunqiu/Documents/Primoria/supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.ts`
  - Add `INTERACTIVE_VISUAL_TWO_STEP_ENABLED` env-flag read at top (default `'true'`).
  - Replace `buildInteractiveVisualPrompt` with a thin compositor that pulls from `prompts/coreSystem.ts` + selected skills + design tokens (used only by render step).

If we skip this, do nothing — the server output is trusted and the client validator only runs on raw artifact reload.

## 4. Plan-step JSON schema

```ts
// supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/planSchema.ts
import { z } from 'npm:zod@3.25.76';

export const PlanSchema = z.object({
  approach: z.string().min(20).max(800),          // one-paragraph design intent
  technology: z.enum(['svg', 'canvas2d', 'three', 'd3', 'chartjs', 'css-anim', 'hybrid']),
  template: z.string().min(2).max(60),            // e.g. 'linear-function', 'wave', '3d-scene'
  palette: z.object({
    mode: z.enum(['light', 'dark', 'auto']).default('auto'),
    primary: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/),
    accent: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/),
    surface: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/).optional(),
  }),
  keyElements: z.array(z.string().min(2)).min(2).max(8),  // e.g. "live formula y=ax+b", "slope triangle"
  interactions: z.array(z.object({
    control: z.string(),                          // 'slider:a', 'button:reset', 'drag:point'
    purpose: z.string(),                          // educational reason
  })).min(1).max(8),
  accessibilityNotes: z.array(z.string()).min(1).max(6),
  observationCopyHint: z.string().max(280),       // what the live observation should say
});
export type Plan = z.infer<typeof PlanSchema>;
```

Example:
```json

  "approach": "Show y = ax + b on a coordinate plane with the line redrawing live as a and b change. Highlight slope via a Δx=1, Δy=a triangle.",

  "template": "linear-function",
  "palette": { "mode": "auto", "primary": "#2563eb", "accent": "#e4572e", "surface": "#ffffff" },
  "keyElements": ["live formula y=ax+b", "labeled axes", "slope triangle", "y-intercept marker"],
  "interactions": [
    {"control": "slider:a", "purpose": "Vary slope to feel rotation/tilt"},
    {"control": "slider:b", "purpose": "Vary intercept to feel parallel shift"},
    {"control": "button:reset", "purpose": "Return to identity line"}
  ],
  "accessibilityNotes": ["sliders have aria-labels", "contrast meets WCAG AA"],
  "observationCopyHint": "When a increases, the line rotates steeper through (0,b)."
}
```

## 5. Render-step prompt structure

Composition order (passed as the user-message text; system instruction stays the safety preamble):

1. `CORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` — global rules: complete HTML doc, no commentary, no fetch, must call `window.PrimoriaInteractive?.track`, must use injected tokens + `iv-*` classes, may use CDN allowlist via `<script type="module">` imports from esm.sh / jsdelivr only.
2. `DESIGN_TOKEN_GUIDE` — table of CSS variable names and what each means (colors, spacing, radius, font), with directive "use `var(--color-...)` for ALL color references; do not hardcode colors".
3. Selected skill prompts (`pickSkillsForTemplate(plan.template, plan.technology)`) — 1–2 of: `linearFunction`, `wave`, `threeDScene`, `chart`, `generic`.
4. Existing `iv-*` class layout guide (the structured paragraph already in `buildInteractiveVisualPrompt`).
5. Locked plan — `Plan JSON (authoritative — implement exactly):\n<json>`.
6. Author context (surface, language, title, description) and the user's original `prompt`.
7. Optional repair note (validator errors + "you must keep the plan above intact").

## 6. New validator rules

CDN allowlist (tight): `https://esm.sh/` and `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/` only. We deliberately exclude unpkg (history of arbitrary subpaths) and skypack.

Changes in `validateOfflineHtml` (current location lines 357–379 of `index.ts`):

- Drop the blanket `<script[^>]+src=` rejection; instead allow `<script type="module" src="https://esm.sh/...">` or `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/...`.
- Drop the blanket `type=module` rejection.
- Drop the blanket "no module imports" rule. **Allow** static `import ... from "https://esm.sh/..."` and `import ... from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/..."` inside module scripts. Still **forbid** `import(...)` dynamic with a non-allowlisted argument — easiest: forbid `import(` entirely (libs we allow don't need dynamic import).
- Keep forbidding `<link href=...>` for stylesheets (no CSS CDN; design tokens come from us).
- Keep forbidding `<iframe|embed|object>`.
- Keep forbidding `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`.
- Replace the "no `https?://` anywhere" check with: after stripping (a) SVG/XLink namespace URLs (already handled), (b) allowlisted CDN URLs that appear only inside `<script src=...>` or `import ... from "..."` positions, any remaining `https?://` is rejected.

Concrete regex sketch (where in `index.ts`):
```ts
const ALLOWED_CDN = /^https:\/\/(esm\.sh|cdn\.jsdelivr\.net\/npm)\//;
// In validateOfflineHtml:
//   1) Collect all <script ... src="X"> X values → each must match ALLOWED_CDN.
//   2) Collect all `import ... from "X"` X values → each must match ALLOWED_CDN.
//   3) Strip allowed-CDN URLs and SVG-namespace URLs from html → assert no remaining https?://.
//   4) Reject dynamic import(): /\bimport\s*\(/i.
//   5) Reject fetch/XHR/WebSocket as today.
```

## 8. Skill files (scope only)

# Interactive Visualization Block — Two-Step Generation Upgrade

## Context

Today the `viewer-ai-interactive-visual` edge function makes **one** Gemini call that must both invent design intent and emit a runnable, strictly-offline HTML document. Quality is capped by the single-shot constraint and by the lack of richer rendering libraries (no Three.js / D3 / GSAP / Chart.js). We are porting four patterns from CopilotKit / OpenGenerativeUI:

1. **Two-step generation**: a `plan` call (structured JSON: approach, technology, palette, key elements, interactions, accessibility, observation hint) feeds a `render` call.
2. **Modular skills**: a small core system prompt + per-template skill modules picked based on the plan.
3. **CDN allowlist** (`esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm`) inside the iframe so generated HTML can `import` `three`, `d3`, `gsap`, `chart.js/auto` via `<script type="module">`. Iframe sandbox stays `allow-scripts`.
4. **Design-token CSS variables** with light + dark mode injected alongside the existing `iv-*` layout classes; AI is instructed to use `var(--color-*)` for color and `iv-*` classes for layout primitives.

Cost roughly doubles per job (two Gemini calls). Accepted as the price of substantially higher visual fidelity. Artifact stays backward compatible — `plan` is an additive field in `result_artifact` JSONB; no DB migration. Both behaviors are gated by env flags so rollback is one variable.

## Architecture

         ├── Step B  generateInteractiveHtml(payload, plan)
         │     skills = pickSkillsForTemplate(plan.template, plan.technology)
         │     prompt = coreSystem + skills + designTokenGuide

         │

               template, experienceMode, themeTone, aiPrompt,

  approach: z.string().min(20).max(800),

  template: z.string().min(2).max(60),

    accent: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/),
    surface: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/).optional(),

  interactions: z.array(z.object({

    purpose: z.string(),     // educational reason

  "interactions": [

    {"control": "slider:b", "purpose": "Vary intercept to feel parallel shift"},
    {"control": "button:reset", "purpose": "Return to identity line"}
  ],

  "observationCopyHint": "When a increases, the line rotates steeper through (0,b)."
}

System instruction (safety preamble) stays unchanged. The user-message text is composed in this order:

- Keep forbidding `<iframe|embed|object>`.
- Keep forbidding `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`.
- Forbid dynamic `import(` entirely (libs we allow are static).
- After stripping (a) SVG/XLink namespace URLs (already handled), (b) allowlisted CDN URLs that occur only in script-src or module-import positions, any remaining `https?://` is rejected.

```ts
const ALLOWED_CDN = /^https:\/\/(esm\.sh|cdn\.jsdelivr\.net\/npm)\//;

// 2) collect `import … from "X"` URLs → each must match ALLOWED_CDN
// 3) strip allowed-CDN + SVG-namespace URLs → no remaining https?:// allowed
// 4) reject /\bimport\s*\(/i
// 5) reject fetch / XMLHttpRequest / WebSocket as today

# Interactive Visualization Block — Two-Step Generation Upgrade

## Context

Today the `viewer-ai-interactive-visual` edge function makes **one** Gemini call that must both invent design intent and emit a runnable, strictly-offline HTML document. Quality is capped by the single-shot constraint and by the lack of richer rendering libraries (no Three.js / D3 / GSAP / Chart.js). We are porting four patterns from CopilotKit / OpenGenerativeUI:

1. **Two-step generation**: a `plan` call (structured JSON: approach, technology, palette, key elements, interactions, accessibility, observation hint) feeds a `render` call.
2. **Modular skills**: a small core system prompt + per-template skill modules picked based on the plan.
3. **CDN allowlist** (`esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm`) inside the iframe so generated HTML can `import` `three`, `d3`, `gsap`, `chart.js/auto` via `<script type="module">`. Iframe sandbox stays `allow-scripts`.
4. **Design-token CSS variables** with light + dark mode injected alongside the existing `iv-*` layout classes; AI is instructed to use `var(--color-*)` for color and `iv-*` classes for layout primitives.

Cost roughly doubles per job (two Gemini calls). Accepted as the price of substantially higher visual fidelity. Artifact stays backward compatible — `plan` is an additive field in `result_artifact` JSONB; no DB migration. Both behaviors are gated by env flags so rollback is one variable.

# Interactive Visualization Block — Two-Step Generation Upgrade

## Context

Today the `viewer-ai-interactive-visual` edge function makes **one** Gemini call that must both invent design intent and emit a runnable, strictly-offline HTML document. Quality is capped by the single-shot constraint and by the lack of richer rendering libraries (no Three.js / D3 / GSAP / Chart.js). We are porting four patterns from CopilotKit / OpenGenerativeUI:

1. **Two-step generation**: a `plan` call (structured JSON: approach, technology, palette, key elements, interactions, accessibility, observation hint) feeds a `render` call.
2. **Modular skills**: a small core system prompt + per-template skill modules picked based on the plan.
3. **CDN allowlist** (`esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm`) inside the iframe so generated HTML can `import` `three`, `d3`, `gsap`, `chart.js/auto` via `<script type="module">`. Iframe sandbox stays `allow-scripts`.
4. **Design-token CSS variables** with light + dark mode injected alongside the existing `iv-*` layout classes; AI is instructed to use `var(--color-*)` for color and `iv-*` classes for layout primitives.

Cost roughly doubles per job (two Gemini calls). Accepted as the price of substantially higher visual fidelity. Artifact stays backward compatible — `plan` is an additive field in `result_artifact` JSONB; no DB migration. Both behaviors are gated by env flags so rollback is one variable.

## Architecture

```
client (Builder / AI-Tutor)
   │ POST action=create
   ▼
edge function: viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.ts
   │
   ├── job row inserted (status=queued)
   │
   └── processSingleJob()
         │
         ├── Step A  generateInteractivePlan(payload)
         │     prompt = coreSystem + planInstructions + user ask
         │     Gemini #1 → JSON
         │     parsePlanText() → PlanSchema (zod)
         │     plan parse fail → retry once with repair note
         │
         ├── Step B  generateInteractiveHtml(payload, plan)
         │     skills = pickSkillsForTemplate(plan.template, plan.technology)
         │     prompt = coreSystem + skills + designTokenGuide
         │              + iv-* layout guide + plan(JSON) + user ask
         │              + optional render-repair note (validator errors + locked plan)
         │     Gemini #2 → HTML
         │     extractInteractiveVisualHtml()
         │     injectInteractiveVisualBaseStyles()   ← also injects design-token block
         │     validateOfflineHtml()                  ← UPDATED allowlist
         │     validation fail → loop ≤ MAX_VALIDATION_REPAIRS, plan stays locked
         │
         └── result_artifact = {
               version, engine, title, description,
               template, experienceMode, themeTone, aiPrompt,
               generatedHtml,
               plan: { …PlanSchema }      ← NEW additive field
             }

client poll (unchanged) reads resultArtifact; older readers ignore plan.
InteractiveVisualEmbed unchanged — same srcDoc iframe, same bridge script.
```

## File-by-file changes

**New files** (Deno-friendly TS string exports inside the edge function dir):

- `supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/prompts/coreSystem.ts` — exports `CORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS`.
- `supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/prompts/designTokens.ts` — exports `DESIGN_TOKEN_CSS`, `DESIGN_TOKEN_GUIDE`.
- `supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/prompts/skills/linearFunction.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/wave.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/threeDScene.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/chart.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/generic.ts`
- `…/prompts/skills/index.ts` — exports `pickSkillsForTemplate(template, technology) → string[]`.
- `…/planSchema.ts` — exports zod `PlanSchema`, `type Plan`, `parsePlanText(raw)`.
- `…/planStep.ts` — `generateInteractivePlan(payload, repairNote?) → Promise<Plan>` (Gemini call #1).
- `…/renderStep.ts` — `generateInteractiveHtml(payload, plan, repairErrors[]) → Promise<artifact>` (Gemini call #2).
- `…/planSchema.test.ts` — parser happy + error paths.

**Modified files**:

- `supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.ts`
  - Read `INTERACTIVE_VISUAL_TWO_STEP_ENABLED` (default `'true'`) and `INTERACTIVE_VISUAL_CDN_ALLOWLIST_ENABLED` (default `'true'`) at top.
  - Replace body of `generateInteractiveVisual()`: when two-step is on → `planStep` then `renderStep`, return `{ artifact, plan }`; when off → current single-call path.
  - Replace `buildInteractiveVisualPrompt()` with a thin composer that pulls `coreSystem + selected skills + designTokenGuide + iv-* guide + plan JSON + user ask` (used only by render step).
  - Update `validateOfflineHtml()` per §6.
  - Update `injectInteractiveVisualBaseStyles()` to also inject `<style data-primoria-visual-tokens>` block from `DESIGN_TOKEN_CSS` before the existing `data-primoria-visual-base` block.
  - Update `artifactResponse()` to include `plan` when present.
  - Update `processSingleJob()` so render-step retries reuse the locked plan rather than re-planning.
  - Update `buildRepairInstruction()` signature to accept an optional plan context for render-step retries.

- `supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.test.ts` — see §10.

**Unchanged**: all `packages/viewer-react/**`, all SQL migrations, `InteractiveVisualEmbed`, `interactiveVisualApi.ts`, `interactiveVisual.ts`, panels, modes.

**Optional client touch-up** (recommended, low-risk): widen `validateOfflineInteractiveHtml` in `packages/viewer-react/src/shared/interactive/interactiveVisual.ts` to mirror the same CDN allowlist so a server-passing HTML doesn't get rejected when re-normalized on the client.

## Plan-step JSON schema

```ts
// supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/planSchema.ts
import { z } from 'npm:zod@3.25.76';

export const PlanSchema = z.object({
  approach: z.string().min(20).max(800),
  technology: z.enum(['svg', 'canvas2d', 'three', 'd3', 'chartjs', 'css-anim', 'hybrid']),
  template: z.string().min(2).max(60),
  palette: z.object({
    mode: z.enum(['light', 'dark', 'auto']).default('auto'),
    primary: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/),
    accent: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/),
    surface: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/).optional(),
  }),
  keyElements: z.array(z.string().min(2)).min(2).max(8),
  interactions: z.array(z.object({
    control: z.string(),     // 'slider:a', 'button:reset', 'drag:point'
    purpose: z.string(),     // educational reason
  })).min(1).max(8),
  accessibilityNotes: z.array(z.string()).min(1).max(6),
  observationCopyHint: z.string().max(280),
});
export type Plan = z.infer<typeof PlanSchema>;
```

Example:
```json
{
  "approach": "Show y = ax + b on a coordinate plane with the line redrawing live as a and b change. Highlight slope via a Δx=1, Δy=a triangle.",
  "technology": "svg",
  "template": "linear-function",
  "palette": { "mode": "auto", "primary": "#2563eb", "accent": "#e4572e", "surface": "#ffffff" },
  "keyElements": ["live formula y=ax+b", "labeled axes", "slope triangle", "y-intercept marker"],
  "interactions": [
    {"control": "slider:a", "purpose": "Vary slope to feel rotation/tilt"},
    {"control": "slider:b", "purpose": "Vary intercept to feel parallel shift"},
    {"control": "button:reset", "purpose": "Return to identity line"}
  ],
  "accessibilityNotes": ["sliders have aria-labels", "contrast meets WCAG AA"],
  "observationCopyHint": "When a increases, the line rotates steeper through (0,b)."
}
```

## Render-step prompt composition

System instruction (safety preamble) stays unchanged. The user-message text is composed in this order:

1. `CORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` — hard rules: complete `<!doctype html>`, no fences, must call `window.PrimoriaInteractive?.track`, must use injected tokens + `iv-*` classes, may `<script type="module">` import only from esm.sh / jsdelivr-npm, no fetch / XHR / WebSocket / dynamic import.
2. `DESIGN_TOKEN_GUIDE` — names + meanings of each CSS variable; directive "use `var(--color-*)` for ALL color references; never hardcode hex".
3. Selected skill prompts (`pickSkillsForTemplate(plan.template, plan.technology)` → 1–2 of `linearFunction`, `wave`, `threeDScene`, `chart`, `generic`).
4. Existing `iv-*` class layout guide (kept verbatim from current `buildInteractiveVisualPrompt`).
5. `Plan JSON (authoritative — implement exactly):\n<json>`.
6. Author context (surface, language, title, description) + the user's original `prompt`.
7. Optional repair note (validator errors + "you must keep the plan above intact").

## Validator rules

CDN allowlist (tight): only `https://esm.sh/` and `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/`. Unpkg and skypack excluded.

Changes inside `validateOfflineHtml()` (current location lines 357–379 of `index.ts`):

- Allow `<script type="module" src="…">` and module `import … from "…"` when URL matches `ALLOWED_CDN`.
- Keep forbidding non-module `<script src>`.
- Keep forbidding `<link href>` stylesheets (no CSS CDN).
- Keep forbidding `<iframe|embed|object>`.
- Keep forbidding `fetch(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`.
- Forbid dynamic `import(` entirely (libs we allow are static).
- After stripping (a) SVG/XLink namespace URLs (already handled), (b) allowlisted CDN URLs that occur only in script-src or module-import positions, any remaining `https?://` is rejected.

Regex sketch:
```ts
const ALLOWED_CDN = /^https:\/\/(esm\.sh|cdn\.jsdelivr\.net\/npm)\//;
// 1) collect script src= URLs → each must match ALLOWED_CDN
// 2) collect `import … from "X"` URLs → each must match ALLOWED_CDN
// 3) strip allowed-CDN + SVG-namespace URLs → no remaining https?:// allowed
// 4) reject /\bimport\s*\(/i
// 5) reject fetch / XMLHttpRequest / WebSocket as today
```

export const CORE_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION = `You are Primoria's senior educational interaction designer and front-end engineer. You generate portfolio-grade interactive HTML for sandboxed learner iframes. Quality bar: smooth animations, professional typography, accessible controls, polished motion. No proof-of-concept output. Never reveal chain of thought.`;

export const CORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT = `
You are Primoria's senior educational interaction designer and front-end engineer.

Quality bar (non-negotiable):
- Portfolio-grade: smooth animations, considered typography, polished spacing, real depth (shadow + radius), responsive layout.
- No proof-of-concept aesthetics. Never ship raw default form controls without styling.
- The core visualization is the hero — it must occupy the largest visual region and be the first thing the learner notices.

Output discipline:
- Return ONE complete, runnable HTML document. Start with <!doctype html> (or <html>). Include <head>, <body>, and inline <script>.
- Do NOT return JSON. Do NOT wrap the HTML in markdown fences. Do NOT add commentary before or after the HTML.
- Reason silently. Do not reveal chain of thought.

Runtime and sandbox:
- The HTML runs inside an iframe sandbox="allow-scripts". No top-level navigation, no popups, no forms.
- A bridge already exposes window.PrimoriaInteractive.track(eventName, payload). Call it on meaningful learner interactions (slider change, button press, mode switch, animation toggle, prediction submitted). Use snake_case event names.
- Allowed libraries via ES module imports from https://esm.sh/ or https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ ONLY:
    import * as THREE from "https://esm.sh/three";
    import { OrbitControls } from "https://esm.sh/three/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js";
    import * as d3 from "https://esm.sh/d3";
    import gsap from "https://esm.sh/gsap";
    import Chart from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js/auto/+esm";
- When importing, use <script type="module"> with static "import ... from" statements. No dynamic import(). No other origins (no unpkg, no skypack, no jsdelivr-anywhere-else).
- Forbidden everywhere: fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, <iframe>, <object>, <embed>, <link rel="stylesheet" href=...>, external images, external fonts, external data URLs.

Design system:
- The page injects two CSS layers before your <head> runs: design tokens (CSS variables) and Primoria's iv-* layout classes.
- Use var(--color-*) for every color. Never hardcode hex colors. Never declare your own font-family at the body level — inherit var(--font-sans) (or use var(--font-display) for hero titles, var(--font-mono) for numerics).
- Use iv-* classes for layout primitives:
    iv-shell           outer container (grid, max-width)
    iv-header          title strip
    iv-kicker          eyebrow above title
    iv-title           hero heading
    iv-subtitle        supporting copy
    iv-layout          two-column visual + controls grid
    iv-card            generic card surface
    iv-visual-card     hosts the SVG/Canvas/Three.js scene
    iv-controls-card   holds sliders and buttons
    iv-observation-card highlighted observation strip (live insight)
    iv-section-title   small section heading
    iv-control / iv-control-row / iv-label / iv-value / iv-formula
    iv-note / iv-conclusion / iv-pill / iv-badge
- You MAY add a small inline <style> for concept-specific geometry, animation, or labels. Do NOT redeclare resets, fonts, body styling, card systems, or design tokens.

Interaction discipline:
- Every control must have a clear educational purpose. No decorative dials.
- Default state is the simplest meaningful configuration.
- When a value changes, update the visual AND a one-sentence live observation referencing the current value.
- Provide a reset affordance when the experience has 3+ controls.
- Keyboard: every interactive element reachable by Tab; visible focus ring using var(--color-focus-ring).
- Accessibility: aria-label or <label for> on every input; min text size 12px; ensure WCAG AA contrast against the chosen surface.

Motion:
- Animations use var(--duration-base) and var(--ease-standard) unless the concept itself dictates a specific tempo.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion: tone down non-essential motion.

Honour the locked plan you receive. It is authoritative for technology choice, palette, template, key elements, and interactions. If a planned detail is impossible, prefer adjusting style over abandoning the element.
`.trim();

export const PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS = `
You are planning an interactive educational visualization. Reason silently. Return ONLY a JSON object — no commentary, no fences.

The JSON must match this exact shape:
{
  "approach": "<1-3 sentences describing the design intent and what the learner will manipulate>",
  "technology": "<one of: svg | canvas2d | three | d3 | chartjs | css-anim | hybrid>",
  "template": "<short kebab-case tag, e.g. linear-function, wave, 3d-scene, bar-chart, force-vectors, generic>",
  "palette": {
    "mode": "<auto | light | dark>",
    "primary": "#rrggbb",
    "accent": "#rrggbb",
    "surface": "#rrggbb"
  },
  "keyElements": ["<2-8 short noun phrases naming what appears on screen>"],
  "interactions": [
    { "control": "<slider:name | button:name | drag:name | toggle:name | select:name>", "purpose": "<short educational reason>" }
  ],
  "accessibilityNotes": ["<1-6 short rules, e.g. 'sliders have aria-labels', 'AA contrast against surface'>"],
  "observationCopyHint": "<<= 280 chars: what the live observation strip should say when the learner changes a control>"
}

Constraints:
- "technology" must be the BEST single choice; pick "three" only when 3D is genuinely warranted; pick "chartjs" only for data charts; default to "svg" for math/geometry, "canvas2d" for physics simulations.
- "palette.primary" is the dominant accent (lines, focused slider). "palette.accent" is the contrasting accent (highlights, comparisons). "palette.surface" is the visualization background — usually a near-white or near-black close to var(--color-background-secondary).
- At least 2 keyElements and 1 interaction.
- Output JSON only. No prose. No markdown.
`.trim();

export const LINEAR_FUNCTION_SKILL = `
Skill: linear-function

Goal: let the learner FEEL how slope a and intercept b change y = ax + b.

Render with SVG (preferred) inside .iv-visual-card. The SVG must scale to its container — set viewBox and preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" and width="100%" height="100%".

Required visual elements:
- Coordinate plane with x and y axes drawn with var(--color-border-strong). Tick marks every integer from -6 to 6 on both axes. Tick labels in var(--color-text-secondary), 12px, var(--font-mono).
- The line y = ax + b drawn with stroke var(--color-accent-primary), stroke-width 3, stroke-linecap round. Animate the d/path attribute change with a 220ms transition so changes feel alive.
- Y-intercept marker: a filled circle of radius 6 at (0, b) using var(--color-accent-primary), with a small label "b = <value>" anchored above the dot.
- Slope triangle: a dashed right triangle attached to the line illustrating Δx=1, Δy=a. Hypotenuse coincides with the line segment, the horizontal leg labelled "1" and the vertical leg labelled "a = <value>". Use var(--color-accent-secondary) for the dashed legs.
- Live formula readout in .iv-formula: render "y = <a> x + <b>" with the actual numbers, tabular-nums, var(--font-mono).

Required controls (use iv-control, iv-control-row, iv-label, iv-value):
- slider:a, range -5 to 5, step 0.1, default 1.
- slider:b, range -5 to 5, step 0.1, default 0.
- button:reset that returns a=1, b=0.

Live observation strip (.iv-observation-card .iv-conclusion):
- When |a| grows, say the line is rotating steeper around (0, b).
- When sign of a flips, say the line is reflecting through (0, b).
- When b changes, say the line is shifting vertically; the y-intercept moves to (0, <b>).
- Keep the sentence under 90 characters. Update on every input.

Tracking: call window.PrimoriaInteractive?.track?.('slider_changed', { control: 'a' | 'b', value }) and 'reset_pressed'.

Do not add unrelated controls (no color pickers, no zoom). Keep the chrome quiet so the line is the hero.
`.trim();

export const WAVE_SKILL = `
Skill: wave / trigonometric explorer

Goal: let the learner manipulate amplitude, frequency, phase, and vertical shift of a sine or cosine wave and see the curve respond live.

Preferred technology: Canvas 2D for smooth animation. SVG is acceptable for static-trace variants.

Required visual elements:
- A wide canvas (aspect ≈ 16:7) hosted inside .iv-visual-card. Background var(--color-background-secondary). Plot area inset by ~12% on each side.
- Faint grid lines using var(--color-border-subtle).
- Axes using var(--color-border-strong) with x labels in radians (-2π, -π, 0, π, 2π) and y labels at -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
- The wave traced with var(--color-accent-primary), stroke-width 3, antialiased. A subtle glow effect by drawing the same path with 50% alpha at stroke-width 8 underneath.
- A leading-edge highlight dot at one sample on the curve, rendered with var(--color-accent-secondary), showing how a moving phase reveals itself as motion.
- Live readouts of amplitude, frequency, phase (radians), shift in a compact 2×2 grid using iv-stat-like cards (use iv-card + iv-section-title).

Required controls inside .iv-controls-card:
- slider:amplitude    range 0.2 to 3.0, step 0.05, default 1.5
- slider:frequency    range 0.25 to 3.0, step 0.05, default 1.0
- slider:phase        range -3.14 to 3.14, step 0.01, default 0
- slider:shift        range -2 to 2, step 0.05, default 0
- slider:speed        range 0 to 2.5, step 0.05, default 1.0
- button:play_pause   toggles animation
- button:reset        returns defaults

Live observation strip:
- Always reference one current parameter. E.g., "Frequency 1.45 makes the wave compress horizontally."
- Update on every input event.

Animation loop:
- Use requestAnimationFrame. Maintain a phase offset advanced by elapsed * speed.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion: when reduced, freeze animation and keep the highlight dot static at phase = current phase.

Tracking: track('slider_changed', { control, value }), 'play_toggled', 'reset_pressed'.
`.trim();

export const THREE_D_SCENE_SKILL = `
Skill: 3d-scene (Three.js)

Goal: render a real WebGL scene that the learner can explore by orbit-dragging, with a single hero mesh tied to the concept.

Hard rules:
- NEVER fake 3D with CSS perspective, CSS transforms, or manual canvas projection. Always use Three.js with PerspectiveCamera + WebGLRenderer.
- Use <script type="module">. Import exactly:
    import * as THREE from "https://esm.sh/three";
    import { OrbitControls } from "https://esm.sh/three/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js";
  Optional:
    import gsap from "https://esm.sh/gsap";
- No other modules. No CDN images. No external textures. Generate procedural geometry and procedural materials.

Required scene contents:
- One hero mesh that represents the concept (atom, molecule, cell, planet, manifold, gear, polyhedron, …). Use MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhysicalMaterial. Set metalness/roughness deliberately.
- Lighting: AmbientLight at low intensity (~0.35) + DirectionalLight (~1.0) from above-front. Optional HemisphereLight for soft ground bounce. Cast shadows ONLY if the concept benefits.
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera 50° fov, positioned to frame the hero with ~20% headroom.
- OrbitControls with enableDamping = true, dampingFactor 0.08, target on hero center. autoRotate optional and slow (≤ 0.6 speed).
- Renderer: WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true }); setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2)); setSize on container; ResizeObserver to keep it responsive.

Required UI:
- The Three.js canvas lives inside .iv-visual-card and fills it.
- Controls inside .iv-controls-card that drive scene parameters relevant to the concept (e.g., bond length, radius, rotation speed, mesh resolution). Each control must visibly change the scene within 220ms.
- A toggle:auto_rotate button.
- A reset:view button that calls controls.reset() and restores defaults.

Materials must reference design tokens for the hero's accent colors:
    const rootStyles = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
    const accent = rootStyles.getPropertyValue('--color-accent-primary').trim();
    material.color = new THREE.Color(accent);

Lifecycle:
- Run an rAF loop. Stop it on visibilitychange hidden. Resume on visible.
- Dispose geometries, materials, and renderer when unloading (window 'beforeunload') to prevent leaks.

Tracking: track('orbit_started') once on first user interaction; track('control_changed', { control, value }) on slider input.

Respect prefers-reduced-motion: disable autoRotate by default if user prefers reduced motion.
`.trim();

Goal: render one clear, accurate chart whose colors and typography come from the injected design tokens, with optional interactivity that helps the learner reason about the data.

    import Chart from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js/auto/+esm";
    </script>

export const GENERIC_SKILL = `
Skill: generic concept explorer

Goal: explain ONE concept with ONE primary interaction. Avoid dashboards. Avoid filler cards.

Layout:
- iv-shell > iv-header (kicker + title + 1-sentence subtitle) > iv-layout

    .iv-visual-card  hero visualization (SVG or Canvas)

    "At angle 60° the projectile peaks higher but lands shorter than at 45°."

Educational copy:
- The header subtitle states the question being explored, in plain language.
- Keep all body copy under 240 characters total. Lean on labels next to elements, not paragraphs.

Tracking: track('control_changed', { control, value }) and 'reset_pressed'.

Forbidden:
- Multiple equal-weight cards. The visualization must dominate.
- Generic placeholder titles like "Demo" or "Visualization".
- Decorative emojis.
`.trim();

## 完成 ✅

### 已交付

- `prompts/designTokens.ts` — CSS 变量设计系统（明/暗双模式）+ 提示词指南

- `planSchema.ts` — zod schema + JSON 解析器（带 fence 剥离、JSON 抽取、详细错误）
- `planStep.ts` — Gemini 调用 #1（生成 plan）
- `renderStep.ts` — Gemini 调用 #2（基于 plan 生成 HTML）
- `geminiCall.ts` — 共享的 `GenerationAttemptError` + Gemini 调用 helper
- `planSchema.test.ts` — 6 个解析器测试

**修改 3 个文件**
- `supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.ts` — 两步流水线编排、CDN 白名单 validator、design token 注入、`iv-*` 类别名设计 token、两个回滚 env flag
- `supabase/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/index.test.ts` — 新增 ESM 允许 / 拒绝 / 动态 import 测试
- `packages/viewer-react/src/shared/interactive/interactiveVisual.ts` — 客户端 validator 镜像同一白名单
- `packages/viewer-react/test/interactiveVisualValidation.test.ts` — 新增 4 个测试

### 质量门禁全过

- ✅ `deno check` — 干净
- ✅ Deno 测试 — **17/17 通过**（包含 11 个 index.test.ts + 6 个 planSchema.test.ts）
- ✅ `pnpm typecheck` — 干净
- ✅ Vitest interactive-visual 测试 — **29/29 通过**（apiValidation + Panel + Renderer + geminiClient）

仓库整体 vitest 还有 2 个 dashboardPage 失败，但**与本次改动无关**（验证：stash 本次改动后失败数变成 13，恢复后只剩 2）。

### 回滚开关

```bash
# 完全回退到旧的单次调用 prompt：
INTERACTIVE_VISUAL_TWO_STEP_ENABLED=false

# 关闭 CDN 白名单（验证器回到严格离线）：
INTERACTIVE_VISUAL_CDN_ALLOWLIST_ENABLED=false
```

下一步建议：在 Supabase 部署 edge function 后，用 builder 跑三个 prompt（`y=ax+b`、`正弦波 振幅 相位`、`奥运奖牌柱状图`）做端到端冒烟，确认 iframe 渲染 + 明暗主题切换 + `PrimoriaInteractive.track` 事件。

碰到两个限制，需要你帮一下：

**Logs follow 不可用** — 你装的 supabase CLI v2.75.0 没有 `functions logs` 子命令（v2.80+ 才加的）。两个办法：
1. 升级 CLI：`brew upgrade supabase`
2. 直接看 Dashboard 实时日志：https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/rygafvlzzkvqhhenajzi/functions/viewer-ai-interactive-visual/logs

**查 error_history** — `.env` 里只有 `SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`，没有 service_role key 或 DB 连接串，所以我没办法直接绕过 RLS 查 `interactive_visual_generation_jobs` 表。三条路：

content.text:
## 原因分析

**直接原因**：plan 步骤的 zod schema 要求 `palette.primary/accent/surface` 是 `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$` 格式（即 `#2563eb` 这种 6 位 hex），但 Gemini 返回的不是这个格式。三个字段同时失败，说明返回的是**一种统一的非 hex 格式**。

**最可能的根因**：我的 prompt 内部有冲突。

在 `prompts/designTokens.ts` 里 `DESIGN_TOKEN_GUIDE` 写着：
> Use them for ALL colors, radii, shadows, spacing, and typography. **Never hardcode hex colors**.

而我在 `prompts/coreSystem.ts` 的 `CORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` 里又强调：
> **Never hardcode hex colors.** Never declare your own font-family at the body level.

但 `PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS` 又要求 palette 字段用 `#rrggbb`：
```
"palette": {
  "primary": "#rrggbb",
  "accent": "#rrggbb",
  ...
}
```

这两条规则在 plan 阶段是矛盾的。Gemini 看到"绝不要硬编码 hex"的反复警告后，在 palette 里大概率返回了下面其中一种：
1. CSS 变量引用："var(--color-accent-primary)"
2. 命名 token："accent-primary"
3. CSS 函数："rgb(37, 99, 235)"
4. 3 位简写："#fff"

**还可能的次要原因**：

- Schema 太严格 —— `#FFFFFF`（大写）我已经允许；但 `#fff`（3 位简写）和 8 位带 alpha（`#ffffffff`）都会拒。AI 输出 3 位简写是常态。

- `surface` 是 `.optional()`，但如果 AI 给了个非法值它仍然失败 —— 不会因为字段可选就跳过校验。

## 我没看到的

`error_history` 里没有保存 Gemini 的原始文本，所以我看不到它具体返回了什么。要确认是哪种情况，最直接的办法是**让 plan 步骤在解析失败时把原始 Gemini 输出也带回来**（写到 job 的 `result_artifact.lastPlanRaw` 或在 error message 里附上前 500 字符）。

## 修复方向（你拍板）

1. **改 prompt**：在 plan 指令里明确划清界限——"在 palette JSON 里**必须**用 6 位 hex 字面量；'never hardcode hex' 只适用于生成的 HTML 里"。
2. **改 schema**：放宽到接受 3/6/8 位 hex + `rgb()/rgba()`，再在用之前 normalize 成 6 位 hex 给 render 步骤。
3. **两者都做**（最稳）：prompt 划清界限 + schema 容忍常见变体。
4. **顺带改可观测性**：在 PlanParseError 抛出前把 Gemini 原始响应的前几百字附在 message 里，下次能直接看到。

我倾向 3 + 4。但要不要等你先用文件验证一下确实是这个原因，再动手？

export const CORE_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION = `You are Primoria's senior educational interaction designer and front-end engineer. You generate portfolio-grade interactive HTML for sandboxed learner iframes. Quality bar: smooth animations, professional typography, accessible controls, polished motion. No proof-of-concept output. Never reveal chain of thought.`;

export const CORE_SYSTEM_PROMPT = `
You are Primoria's senior educational interaction designer and front-end engineer.

Quality bar (non-negotiable):
- Portfolio-grade: smooth animations, considered typography, polished spacing, real depth (shadow + radius), responsive layout.
- No proof-of-concept aesthetics. Never ship raw default form controls without styling.
- The core visualization is the hero — it must occupy the largest visual region and be the first thing the learner notices.

Output discipline:
- Return ONE complete, runnable HTML document. Start with <!doctype html> (or <html>). Include <head>, <body>, and inline <script>.
- Do NOT return JSON. Do NOT wrap the HTML in markdown fences. Do NOT add commentary before or after the HTML.
- Reason silently. Do not reveal chain of thought.

Runtime and sandbox:
- The HTML runs inside an iframe sandbox="allow-scripts". No top-level navigation, no popups, no forms.
- A bridge already exposes window.PrimoriaInteractive.track(eventName, payload). Call it on meaningful learner interactions (slider change, button press, mode switch, animation toggle, prediction submitted). Use snake_case event names.
- Allowed libraries via ES module imports from https://esm.sh/ or https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ ONLY:
    import * as THREE from "https://esm.sh/three";
    import { OrbitControls } from "https://esm.sh/three/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js";
    import * as d3 from "https://esm.sh/d3";
    import gsap from "https://esm.sh/gsap";
    import Chart from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js/auto/+esm";
- When importing, use <script type="module"> with static "import ... from" statements. No dynamic import(). No other origins (no unpkg, no skypack, no jsdelivr-anywhere-else).
- Forbidden everywhere: fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, <iframe>, <object>, <embed>, <link rel="stylesheet" href=...>, external images, external fonts, external data URLs.

Design system:
- The page injects two CSS layers before your <head> runs: design tokens (CSS variables) and Primoria's iv-* layout classes.
- Use var(--color-*) for every color. Never hardcode hex colors. Never declare your own font-family at the body level — inherit var(--font-sans) (or use var(--font-display) for hero titles, var(--font-mono) for numerics).
- Use iv-* classes for layout primitives:
    iv-shell           outer container (grid, max-width)
    iv-header          title strip
    iv-kicker          eyebrow above title
    iv-title           hero heading
    iv-subtitle        supporting copy
    iv-layout          two-column visual + controls grid
    iv-card            generic card surface
    iv-visual-card     hosts the SVG/Canvas/Three.js scene
    iv-controls-card   holds sliders and buttons
    iv-observation-card highlighted observation strip (live insight)
    iv-section-title   small section heading
    iv-control / iv-control-row / iv-label / iv-value / iv-formula
    iv-note / iv-conclusion / iv-pill / iv-badge
- You MAY add a small inline <style> for concept-specific geometry, animation, or labels. Do NOT redeclare resets, fonts, body styling, card systems, or design tokens.

Interaction discipline:
- Every control must have a clear educational purpose. No decorative dials.
- Default state is the simplest meaningful configuration.
- When a value changes, update the visual AND a one-sentence live observation referencing the current value.
- Provide a reset affordance when the experience has 3+ controls.
- Keyboard: every interactive element reachable by Tab; visible focus ring using var(--color-focus-ring).
- Accessibility: aria-label or <label for> on every input; min text size 12px; ensure WCAG AA contrast against the chosen surface.

Motion:
- Animations use var(--duration-base) and var(--ease-standard) unless the concept itself dictates a specific tempo.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion: tone down non-essential motion.

Honour the locked plan you receive. It is authoritative for technology choice, palette, template, key elements, and interactions. If a planned detail is impossible, prefer adjusting style over abandoning the element.
`.trim();
